Conversation, family & daily routines

kiss noun and verb

also peck, little kiss

classical

Traupman 336

bāsium, bāsiī n.

noun, second declension

a kiss

Other words

  • bāsiō, bāsiāre, bāsiāvī, bāsiātum

    verb, first conjugation · classical · Traupman 62; Traupman 336

  • ōsculum, ōsculī n. — a kiss

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 336

    Another ancient word for a kiss.

  • ōsculor, ōsculārī, ōsculātus sum — to kiss

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Traupman 336

  • suāvior (sāvior), suāviārī, suāviātus sum — to kiss

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 16.3.6: Atticam nostram cupiō absentem suāviārī (Lewis & Short); Traupman 336

  • bāsiolum, bāsiolī n. — a little kiss, a peck

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Petr. 85 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 358

Examples

  • Vīs bāsium?

    Would you like a kiss?composed

  • Bāsium mihi dā.

    Give me a kiss.composed

  • suāvium alicui dare

    to give someone a kissTraupman 336

See also hug, I love you.
